task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 21, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style news update on changes to Wrenstack Distribution's bookstore order terms and their likely practical effects for small shops and publishers.

facts.text: Wrenstack Distribution notified its bookstore customers on Friday, Aug. 21, 2026, that new order terms begin Oct. 1.
Stores will be able to combine books from different represented publishers in one shipment to reach a 50-copy freight-free threshold.
Orders below 50 copies will carry a $15 shipping charge, regardless of the books' combined retail value.
The old arrangement required 25 copies from each individual publisher for that publisher's shipment to qualify for free freight.
Wrenstack represents 38 small publishers and supplies 214 independent shops in its region.
Book trade discounts and the existing return window are unchanged by the shipping policy.
Distribution director Fenna Sore said mixed-publisher packing was made possible by a new shared warehouse inventory system.
The company has not released an estimate of aggregate bookstore savings or additional warehouse labor costs.
Elbow Lane Books currently orders about 60 copies a week spread across six Wrenstack publishers, according to owner Teri Moss.
Moss expects one mixed shipment to reduce the number of small deliveries she must receive and unpack.
Dune Pocket Books often orders ten or fewer copies for customer requests and does not have room to hold large spare stocks.
Dune Pocket owner Ivo Keld said waiting to build a 50-copy order could slow special orders.
Keld said, "The shelf space is real money too, even when the delivery line says free."
Wrenstack will permit shops to keep an open combined order for up to seven calendar days before dispatch.
Shops can request dispatch before the seven-day limit; the $15 charge applies only if that shipment contains fewer than 50 copies.
Small publisher Asha Vale said a mixed order could place her slower-selling poetry titles beside larger publishers' releases.
Vale said, "I want the book to travel with the order, not wait until it can fill a box by itself."
Wrenstack has scheduled two customer webinars but is not requiring shops to use automated reordering.
Its warehouse employs 31 people and occupies a former wholesale-fabric building.
The policy applies only to represented publishers' books, not every title a participating bookstore sells.

forbidden_additions: A threshold based on dollar value or free shipping for every special order
Changed trade discounts, mandatory automated ordering or measured savings not released
